answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through topological cut verifications and multi-agent auditing: nodes deposit staked value before broadcasting work. If a peer routes traffic via an isolated cluster acting like a jetty off the core trust graph, verifiers evaluate the cut metric. A randomized audit inspects encrypted cipher commitments, matching outputs like lines of a deterministic sonnet. Malicious cartels face stake slashing, enforcing a superlinear attacker cost.
